one_liner: Senior manager at ODNI's National Counterintelligence and Security Center leading an interagency team that coordinates U.S. counterintelligence strategy, governance and senior-level briefings.
fit_summary: This GS-15 role demands expert knowledge of counterintelligence missions, authorities and Intelligence Community organizations, plus SCI eligibility, and Daniel's known background is emergency-management consulting and strong policy knowledge, not counterintelligence or IC leadership. Daniel's relationship-building and interagency coordination skills are relevant, but they are unlikely to clear the expert-level CI/IC bar for a senior leadership position. Lower-grade policy or preparedness roles would be far better targets.
eligibility: Open to the public (excepted service), so Daniel may apply without federal status; current federal employees below GS-14 are ineligible.
Requires at least a bachelor's degree. Confirm Daniel holds one and can document it.
Requires a Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) clearance with investigation and likely polygraph. Daniel has no known clearance.
The posting expects expert knowledge of counterintelligence missions, authorities and IC organizations, plus superior leadership of interagency working groups.
All applicants must answer four essay questions (200 words max each), written in their own words without consultant or AI help.
strategy: Decide honestly whether to spend effort here. Unless Daniel has real counterintelligence or IC work, treat this as a stretch application and put most energy into GS-11 to GS-13 policy, preparedness or legislative-affairs roles.

If you do apply, describe your IEM work in terms of interagency coordination: [federal/state/local clients], governance or working groups you supported, and briefings delivered to senior officials. Use the posting's exact language only where it is truthful.
Keep the resume to the two-page USAJOBS limit. For each job, list dates, hours per week, and one or two lines tying the work to strategy, governance, lessons learned and senior briefings.
Write the four essays yourself, each under 200 words, with concrete examples. The posting forbids consultant or AI drafting, so use these notes only as a checklist.
Submit before November 12, 2026, with your transcript or degree proof and every item under Required Documents. Upload nothing extra.
resume_bullets: Coordinated [number] [federal/state/local] partner agencies on [preparedness/recovery project] for [client], leading [working group/meetings] that resolved [type of issue] by [date/outcome].
Prepared and delivered [number] briefings and reports for [senior official titles] on [topic], producing recommendations adopted in [plan/policy name].
Led [after-action review/lessons-learned assessment] for [exercise/event], identifying [number] improvements implemented under [budget/resource constraint].
interview_questions: Describe how you led an interagency group with competing authorities toward a shared decision.
How would you brief a senior policymaker on a complex threat with limited time?
Tell us about a time you implemented leadership direction that differed from your recommendation.
What do you know about NCSC's mission and the counterintelligence authorities of IC elements?
watch_outs: GS-15 with expert counterintelligence and IC requirements; Daniel's known background does not show this, so referral is unlikely.
TS/SCI clearance is required, with a lengthy investigation and possibly a polygraph.
No telework is offered. The job is on-site in Bethesda, a long commute from Manassas.
The application window is short (October 28 to November 12, 2026), and the essays are mandatory.
